productSurfaces.name: Portable Haxe-to-Go compiler conformance
claims: Ordinary Haxe source preserves the exact operation/member semantics admitted by the compatibility manifest on its named toolchain and platform matrix.
The portable preset is the default product path; a green native or example lane cannot widen this claim.
authoredInputs: ordinary Haxe source without target-native APIs

profileQualifications.metal: Portable semantic preset-invariance evidence only; it is not Go-native API evidence.

upstreamOracleAndPin: Haxe 4.3.7 behavior through --interp where the same source has a faithful portable contract
adaptations: three-family pinned official target smoke with explicitly recorded target and assertion adapters
complete pinned tests/unit owner inventory with provenance-recorded typed harness adapters
knownSkips: 480 applicable owners are explicitly blocked by named compiler, generated-Go, runtime, environment, compile-only-observer, or harness-support gaps
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: commit 7188fea2, CI Harness run 30666284175 and CI - Quality run 30666284172
residualRisks: The extended inventory executes 650 active test methods across 607 owners; its 480 blocked owners remain gaps rather than conformance passes.
The inventory is Linux cold evidence in R4/R5 and does not replace the fast required-PR smoke.
Only explicitly admitted compatibility operations contribute to the beta claim.

productSurfaces.name: Go-native interop and metal policy preset
claims: Typed go.* APIs, extern metadata, and @:goNative boundaries behave as proved by their own fixtures.
Metal is a convenience policy preset, not a second semantic product and not portable-conformance evidence.
authoredInputs: Haxe modules with explicit typed Go-native authority
upstreamOracleAndPin: Go language and standard-library contracts for the exact supported Go versions
adaptations: typed extern and framework-owned go.* facades
productSurfaces.fullBackstopCommand: npm run test:ci && npm run security:go-tooling
residualRisks: Whole go.* classes and unlisted ABI shapes are not admitted by nearby portable evidence.

productSurfaces.name: Generated runtime and staged standard-library behavior
claims: Staged std behavior and typed hxrt resource ownership are supported only for operations named by the compatibility manifest.
Compile-only and cross-build results do not become runtime admission.
upstreamOracleAndPin: Haxe 4.3.7 std behavior where differential execution is faithful
adaptations: canonical std/go/_std overrides and typed std/hxrt bindings
knownSkips: target-sensitive surfaces intentionally kept out of semantic diff
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: commit 7188fea2, CI Harness run 30666284175 and supported-Go tooling jobs
residualRisks: Snapshot/runtime evidence and semantic-diff evidence remain distinct support levels.

productSurfaces.name: Diagnostics, reports, source correlation, and development tooling
claims: Exact negative diagnostics, deterministic compiler reports, and documented developer commands behave as their own tests show.
No source-map claim exists unless an explicit source-map owner is added here.
knownSkips: source maps are not a current public admission
residualRisks: Windows process lifecycle remains compile-only; undeclared custom macro inputs require an explicit --watch-dir.

productSurfaces.name: Package, downstream consumer, and executable examples
claims: The release ZIP installs in isolation and the maintained examples compile, pass strict Go checks, execute, and match manually reviewed output at their declared tiers.
An example proves only its listed profiles, product surfaces, and execution mode.
Only release-bearing lanes may publish portable-beta operation evidence, and every operation must resolve to a release-admitted compatibility entry.
upstreamOracleAndPin: public package layout and release policy
adaptations: CI HXML variants exercise declared application variants
knownSkips: no external third-party downstream corpus yet
productSurfaces.fullBackstopCommand: npm run test:examples && npm run test:haxelib-release-install
productSurfaces.lastCleanProof: commit 7188fea2, Examples Artifacts run 30666284200 and CI Harness run 30666284175

portfolio.method: Count stable behavior owners, not files, assertions, or CI minutes. Overlapping owners are not forced into a percentage.
portfolio.interpretation: The compiler portfolio has a large focused generated-shape base and substantial real Haxe-to-Go execution. Exact ratio publication is deferred until overlapping semantic-diff, runtime, and example owners have stable non-overlapping identities. Static, policy, security, freshness, and schema checks stay outside the ratio.

affectedSelection.selectorMissPolicy: Any R4 failure that should have been selected is recorded as a selector miss, expands the responsible owner mapping, and resets its observation window.
affectedSelection.flakePolicy: Deterministic compiler, assertion, target-build, and runtime failures are never retried into green. Infrastructure reruns preserve the first failure. Quarantine requires an owner, Bead, reason, evidence, and expiry and never contributes a compatibility pass.

questions: Was the test red for the intended reason?
Are negative and boundary cases missing?
Does a mock erase the claimed boundary?
Can the affected selector omit the owner?
Does one product surface launder another surface's result?

representativeWorkflow.kind: documented dry-run of an actual recent regression
representativeWorkflow.protectedClaim: A failed or superseded native socket operation cannot publish or retain a resource, and finite readiness timeouts remain bounded.

scenario.preconditions: An in-progress or failed TCP/TLS/listener/readiness operation owns a native resource behind SocketHandle.
scenario.action: Close, fail policy installation or handshake, or call finite Socket.select beside an entered read.
scenario.observableResult: No stale resource is attached; the exact acquired resource closes; finite select returns within its allowance.
scenario.errorEdgeBehavior: The original typed Haxe-visible failure escapes and a stale failure cannot detach a replacement.

redState.expectedFailure: stale listener state, attached failed TLS connection, and a 20 ms select blocked beyond 150 ms

oracle.source: Haxe socket lifecycle contract, Go resource-ownership invariants, and an independent GPT-5.6 Pro exact-commit review
